rationale: Early-stage startup founders and marketing leads are a nameable buyer segment who demonstrably pay for web presence tools, and the pain (AI-generated sites that hurt conversions) is real and growing. The service — an automated performance audit and fix report for vibe-coded sites — is genuinely buildable with Claude (analyze HTML/CSS/Lighthouse output, generate a prioritized fix report, deliver as PDF or email) and can run with minimal operator involvement after a self-serve intake form. The total clears the validate threshold, all build gates are met, but with zero responsiveness signal and a fairly weak defensibility story, validate (not build) is the right next step.
solution_plan: WHAT: An automated web performance audit service for AI-generated startup marketing sites — the operator submits a URL, gets back a scored report with specific fixes ranked by conversion impact. BUILD: The factory sets up a Typeform (or simple HTML form) intake, a Stripe payment link (~$49/audit), and a Claude pipeline that runs Lighthouse-equivalent checks (via a headless browser API like Browserless or PageSpeed Insights API), then generates a plain-English fix report with prioritized recommendations. No coding by Youval. SELL: Reach founders via HN Show HN posts, Indie Hackers, and Twitter/X threads about vibe-coding — a targeted cold-email or post campaign goes out only after Youval approves the batch. MAINTAIN: Stripe handles billing, the intake form triggers the Claude pipeline automatically, the report is emailed to the customer — Youval's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches. VALIDATE FIRST: Before building, post a landing page with a Stripe link and drive 50 targeted visits to see if anyone converts at $49.
notes: All build gates technically met (operational_autonomy=7, buildability_with_ai=8, buyer_clarity=6, willingness_to_pay=5), but responsiveness_signal=2 (untested) and defensibility=3 mean validate is the right stage. The headless browser API dependency adds minor integration friction worth confirming is automatable before committing to build.
